paragraphs.text: SSH remote workspaces for DeepSeek Harness
# DeepSeek Harness SSH Toolkit
English · 中文

Run DeepSeek Harness sessions on a remote machine over SSH. Pick any folder on
that machine as a wor

kspace, and every shell / file / search tool call executes
there instead of on your laptop.

An independent, DSH 0.2-native continuation of
dsh-ssh/dsh-ssh — see
CREDITS. Not a mirror of upstre

ent, DSH 0.2-native continuation of
dsh-ssh/dsh-ssh — see
CREDITS. Not a mirror of upstream commits.
## Why this one

- **Works on current DSH (0.2.x).** Hosts live in a real storage domain, the
client uses the 0.2 Typ

ert + primitives contracts, and the settings page is
built from the current component set.
- **Impor

t the hosts you already have.** The scanner reads `~/.ssh/config`,
`~/.ssh/config.d/*` and `Include`

chains — the same file VS Code Remote-SSH
uses — and imports user, port and key path in one click.

- **One package, no monorepo.** Host code, client bundle, tests and docs in a
small, navigable tree.

- **Same-name tools, zero prompt surgery.** `bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`,
`read_image`, `glob` a

nd `grep` keep their official names and arguments;
routing depends only on the session's cwd.
## Features
| **Host manager** | Add, edit, test (through the jump chain), remove hosts from Settings → SSH Conn

ections, including an optional jump host. Password is write-only in the UI. |
| **Workspace identity
** | Remote workspace rows carry an online/offline dot, a server icon and the host as a tag; the dir

ectory picker filters as you type and keeps a fixed width. |
| **Update check** | Settings → SSH sho
ws the installed version and flags a newer repository tag with a Release link (checked at most once

per 6 hours). |
| **Jump hosts** | Chain hops through `ProxyJump` host references (cycle-checked), o
r run an OpenSSH-style `ProxyCommand` locally; the terminal follows the same chain with `ssh -J` / `

-o ProxyCommand`. |
| **Config import** | Scans `~/.ssh/config` (+ `config.d`, `Include`) and import

s in bulk; entries without a `User` are flagged instead of silently broken. |
| **Seven routed tools
** | `bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`, `read_image`, `glob`, `grep` — same schemas, executed over SSH

. |
| **Remote workspaces** | Browse a remote directory, pick it, get a local placeholder workspace;

deleting the workspace cleans the placeholder up. |
| **Uploads** | Attaching a file in a remote wo
rkspace writes the bytes into the remote directory (collision-safe names) while keeping the message

attachment card. |
| **UI parity** | The Files sidebar lists/previews the remote tree over SFTP, and
the Terminal panel opens a remote shell (`ssh -tt`), reusing the official terminal for resize/scrol

lback. |
| **Background jobs** | `run_in_background` plus `job_list` / `job_output` / `job_kill` run

on the remote host. |
| **Sandbox parity** | The three sandbox modes fence remote tool calls the sa

me way they fence local ones. |
| **Trust on first use** | Unknown host keys show a fingerprint dial

og; later connections verify `known_hosts`. |
| **Resilient transport** | Connection pool with recon
nect, atomic remote writes, SFTP → `exec`+base64 fallback. |
## Requirements

| DSH | 0.2.1-rc.4 – 0.2.x (rc.5 tested, rc.4 audited) |
| Node | ≥ 22 |
| Remote OS | Linux or macO

S (`sshd` only, no agent to install) |
| Auth | key (path or ssh-agent) or password |
| Topology | m
ulti-hop via `ProxyJump` or `ProxyCommand` |
## Install
From a checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
or straight from GitHub:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Use `--profile web` for a headless web setup. If pnpm reports
`ERR_PNPM_ADDING_TO_ROOT`, append `-w`

. Then **fully restart DSH** and open
Settings → SSH Connections.

The plugin is additive: local workspaces behave exactly as before, and removing
it (`dsh plugin --pr
ofile desktop remove dsh-ssh-toolkit`) leaves DSH untouched.

Updates are manual: DSH only offers its own Update button to official plugins, so
pull/reinstall the

package and fully restart. Settings → SSH shows the installed
version and turns the footer into "Up

date available: vX.Y.Z" when a newer tag
exists on the repository (checked at most once per 6 hours)

ate available: vX.Y.Z" when a newer tag
exists on the repository (checked at most once per 6 hours).

Install the version you want from its tag, or from the `.tgz` attached to the
GitHub release (the au

to-generated "Source code" archives on that page are not
installable packages):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

If the profile refuses to replace an already-installed copy, remove it first
(`dsh plugin --profile
desktop remove dsh-ssh-toolkit`) and add the new one.

If pnpm stops with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` / "Ignored build scripts:
cpu-features, ssh2", the prof

ile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` has undecided build
entries. Decide them explicitly and re-run the insta

ll (ssh2 works without the
optional native addon, so `false` is the quick path; `true` needs a C++ t

orks without the
optional native addon, so `false` is the quick path; `true` needs a C++ toolchain):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

For a `link:`/checkout install (the development setup), `git pull` in the
checkout is the update; th
e client bundle is read from disk on the next start.
## Quick start

1. Settings → SSH Connections → **Import from ~/.ssh/config** (or **Add host**).
2. Test the connect

ion once; confirm the host key fingerprint on first use.
3. New session → pick the host → browse to

a folder → it becomes the workspace.
4. Everything the agent runs now happens on that machine.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Hosts are stored as records in the `dsh_ssh_hosts` storage domain
(`~/.dsh/storages/dsh_ssh_hosts.js

on`). The settings page talks to the host over
a small Typert remote (`ssh/listHosts`, `saveHost`, `

deleteHost`,
`testConnection`, `scanSshConfig`, plus the remote-workspace calls), so no
settings nam
espace is exposed to the wire.
## Notes and limits

- Passwords are stored **in plaintext** in `dsh_ssh_hosts.json` (same trade-off
as upstream). Prefer

keys; the private key itself is never copied.
- Terminal jump chains use the local `ssh -J`, so hop
credentials come from your system ssh config/agent (the stored password applies to the target only)

.
- `ProxyCommand` runs a local `/bin/sh` command from your host configuration — the same trust mode

l as OpenSSH. It is never executed for a host you did not configure.
- Remote `grep` uses GNU grep,

so ignore rules differ slightly from `rg`.
- Windows remotes are not supported.
